reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it favorably presents paid mining packages, affiliate recruitment, binary compensation, commissions, and income claims through an instructional office walkthrough with purchase buttons and team-bonus pages. The supplied records do not establish actual purchases, payouts, full terms, or whether the displayed claims were fulfilled.

opening.argument: The walkthrough includes a visible operational limitation rather than presenting an unqualified success story: the account interface warns that internal-wallet payments are temporarily disabled while integration work is completed. That disclosure gives viewers a material caution about current functionality. The narration also describes the Bitcoin resource as general information, which supports an informational framing rather than a guarantee of profit. Nothing in the supplied material states that returns are certain, that participation is risk-free, or that viewers will definitely earn money.

citations.quote: How to buy Bitcoin? This is general information, VTC.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of purchase buttons and team tools does not by itself establish deceptive solicitation. The cited registration language shows how an account function works, while the compensation-plan reference identifies where information is located; neither quote promises a return or claims that anyone will profit. The visible payment notice further shows that the system discloses a current limitation.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warning is only a temporary payment-status notice; it does not warn that mining returns or commissions may be unavailable or misleading. Calling Bitcoin information general does not neutralize the video’s promotion of paid pools and team compensation. The material still directs viewers through registration, affiliate promotion, and purchasable mining options.

opening.argument: The strongest reading is an operational tutorial. The title identifies office management, the description says it explains how to manage a BitClub back office, and the narration proceeds through menus, registration fields, resources, team views, wallets, and purchase pages. The speaker explicitly calls the presentation a quick review intended to be useful. Showing where features are located and explaining what they do is not the same as certifying the underlying business or promising an outcome.

How to manage your BitClub Network office or backoffice.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s description relies on what the interface contains, not on an explicit sales pitch. The narration calls the content a review and explains navigation through existing account sections. Even the affiliate-link passage can describe a tool’s function without proving that the presenter is guaranteeing results or concealing risks. The records do not establish that viewers were told to purchase or that any outcome was promised.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The format is tutorial-like, but the tutorial explains how to register partners, use an affiliate link, understand income-generating compensation, and buy mining pools. Calling it a review does not change those substantive functions. The instructional presentation is precisely how the promotional mechanisms are made usable; it need not include a verbal guarantee to promote participation.

opening.argument: The material can be understood as ordinary account and product-service promotion, with the presenter explaining available options rather than demonstrating a scam mechanism. The pools are displayed as selectable offerings with stated prices and mining duration, and the dashboard includes ordinary wallet and account-management functions. Crucially, the supplied evidence does not show an actual deposit, a completed purchase, a guaranteed return, a confirmed payout, or credentials being solicited from viewers. It also does not establish that the presenter’s team figures represent income earned by the audience.

rebuttal.rebuttal: A listed price and a purchase control establish that an offering is presented, but they do not establish fraud. The team tree and compensation pages likewise show account features, not proof of a deposited fee, a completed payout, or a guaranteed return. The prosecution’s own framing acknowledges that the records do not establish actual purchases or payouts, leaving the alleged scam mechanism unproven.

Those are not merely neutral wallet functions, even if the supplied material cannot prove a completed payout.
